<details class="mk-bio">
<summary>Full biography</summary>
<p>I graduated from Korea University with an M.D. and a B.A. in Sociology with a minor in Economics, and received an M.P.P. from the KDI School. During my undergraduate years, I served as the Vice President of the Korea University Undergraduate Student Union, where I actively engaged in university and community governance, focusing on youth housing and education policy issues. After graduation, I completed my internship and residency in Preventive Medicine at Korea University Medical Center and pursued a Ph.D. in Public Health at Korea University Graduate School.</p>
<p>During my residency, I became deeply involved in health policy and healthcare workforce advocacy. I served as the President of the Korean Intern Resident Association (KIRA), where I led efforts to improve working conditions and mental health for young doctors. I acted as the Principal Investigator for “A Study on Reforming the 36-hour Consecutive Shift System for Medical Intern and Resident” (Research Institute for Healthcare Policy, Korean Medical Association), and my efforts contributed to crucial reforms in resident working-hour regulations. For my work as KIRA President and Director of Policy at the Korean Medical Association, I received a commendation from the Minister of Health and Welfare in April 2023. I also represented Korean junior doctors internationally as a member of the Korean delegation to the World Medical Association – Junior Doctors Network (WMA-JDN). During these years I also contributed to public health crisis management at the COVID-19 Community Treatment Center in Seoul and served as a visiting researcher at the National Center for Mental Health.</p>
<p>After obtaining my board certification in Preventive Medicine, I began my military service. I am currently serving as an occupational health physician at the Armed Forces Capital Hospital, a military officer in the Department of Healthcare Management of the Armed Forces Medical Command (AFMC), and an epidemiologist at the Ministry of National Defense (MND). In this position, I publish the Military Health Statistics Annual Report and analyse quarterly hospital utilisation and quality indicators to identify policy priorities. In this role, I was also a co-investigator on the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (KDCA) project “Improving Infectious Disease Response and Management Capabilities in the Korean Military”. My research projects examine the determinants of mental health and patterns of healthcare use among military personnel.</p>
<p>My primary research lies at the intersection of social epidemiology and social policy. I develop methodological and applied research to understand how social inequalities — such as precarious employment, long working hours, and area deprivation — translate into adverse health and mental health outcomes. My recent publications have addressed gender inequalities in mental health during the COVID-19 pandemic and the impact of South Korea's national gastrointestinal cancer screening programme. I am currently completing my doctoral dissertation, which examines, in three studies, the associations of working hours, consecutive shifts, and precarious employment with depressive symptoms and suicidal ideation.</p>
<p>Beyond research, I have sought to contribute to community medicine and institutional reform. I currently serve as a Board Member and the Chairperson of the Future Generations Committee for the Korean Society for Preventive Medicine (KSPM), as well as the Vice President and Founding Member of the Korean Association of Preventive Medicine Physicians (KAPMP). Through these roles, and my earlier participation in multiple Ministry of Health and Welfare advisory committees, I continue to strive for practical, preventive approaches to resolve structural issues and build a cohesive society where diverse individuals can thrive together.</p>
